classification.difficultyReason: Model the edging including two internal dividers, eliminate a variable and interpret both positive quadratic solutions.

content.prompt:
A gardener decides to subdivide a rectangular garden bed of area $30\text{ m}^2$ into three equal sections.

He places edging along the outside of the garden bed and as dividers between each section. It takes $32\text{ m}$ of edging. Each section of garden has length $y$ metres (which is also the length of each divider) and width $x$ metres.

spec.sourceRegion: Challenge exercise question 4, diagram to the right of the stem
spec.description: Unshaded rectangle divided by two full-height vertical lines into three adjacent equal sections. Each top segment is labelled x m; the right side is labelled y m. Source blue ordinary strokes are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: The whole garden has dimensions 3x by y. Its outside boundary and two internal dividers require 6x+4y metres of edging.
spec.answerVisibility: All outlines, dividers and dimension labels are permanent givens; no answers are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Express the area of the entire garden bed in terms of $x$.

answer.worked:
The edging includes two horizontal sides and four lengths of $y$.

$$\begin{align*}6x+4y&=32\\4y&=32-6x\\y&=8-\frac32x\end{align*}$$
The whole garden has width $3x$, so its area in square metres is
$$\begin{align*}A&=3xy\\A&=3x\left(8-\frac32x\right)\\A&=24x-\frac92x^2\\A&=\frac12(48x-9x^2).\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the dimensions of the garden bed.

answer.short:
$10\text{ m}\times3\text{ m}$ or $6\text{ m}\times5\text{ m}$.

Set the area expression equal to $30$, factorise and use both positive solutions.
answer.worked:
Using the area of $30\text{ m}^2$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac12(48x-9x^2)&=30\\48x-9x^2&=60\\9x^2-48x+60&=0\\3x^2-16x+20&=0\\3x^2-10x-6x+20&=0\\x(3x-10)-2(3x-10)&=0\\(x-2)(3x-10)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law,
$$\begin{align*}x-2&=0\quad\text{or}\quad3x-10=0\\x&=2\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{10}{3}.\end{align*}$$
If $x=2$,
$$\begin{align*}3x&=6\\y&=8-\frac32(2)\\y&=5.\end{align*}$$
If $x=\frac{10}{3}$,
$$\begin{align*}3x&=10\\y&=8-\frac32\left(\frac{10}{3}\right)\\y&=3.\end{align*}$$
The garden bed is $6\text{ m}\times5\text{ m}$ or $10\text{ m}\times3\text{ m}$. Both have area $30\text{ m}^2$. Their edging totals are respectively $2(6)+4(5)=32\text{ m}$ and $2(10)+4(3)=32\text{ m}$.
